newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Peace talks in Bangladesh end without deal.
newsitem.headline: Peace talks in Bangladesh end without deal.

text.p: Peace talks aimed at ending a decades-old insurgency in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts ended on Thursday without a deal, but government and rebel negotiators said they would meet again on April 30.

"We had discussions in a very cordial atmosphere. We agreed to continue our efforts," the government's chief negotiator Abdul Hasnat Abdullah told reporters at the end of a two-day meeting with a five-member rebel team in Dhaka.
Abdullah said both sides had also agreed to extend the ceasefire in the hill tracts until June 30.
The current ceasefire is due to expire on March 31.
A team of rebel Shanti Bahini (peace force) leaders, led by Jyotirindra Budhipriya Larma, flew to the capital on Wednesday for their second meeting with government leaders since January.
Abdullah, chief parliamentary whip of the ruling Awami League, declined to say why Thursday's talks, the fourth since the government of Sheikh Hasina took power in June 1996, ended without a deal.
One government official, however, said the two sides failed to reach consensus on the question of the fate of Bengali settlers in the troubled hill districts.

The Shanti Bahini has fought a bush war in the 14,200 sq-km (5,500 sq-mile) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, over demands for political autonomy and expulsion of about 500,000 Bengali-speaking settlers from the area.
Over 8,500 rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, according to official figures.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina on Wednesday ruled out a relocation of the Bengali settlers.
Opposition leaders criticise the government for jeopardising the interests of the Bengali settlers, who constitute about 49 percent of the total hill population.
